description: Native decay + identity dynamics, closing two of consumer 6's three named blockers (CAN_CONSUMER_MIGRATION_RESULTS.md Sec1 row 6: 'decay ... no native analog proposed anywhere'; 'identity dynamics ... no native design exists at all'; Blocker B (Hebbian materialization) is a SIBLING rung's exact scope, not touched here). DECAY: the continuous mt_decay_h/mt_decay_J (can_ops.rs) are multiplicative (h <- (1-gamma)*h) -- a category error applied to an in-frame integer count (0.999*7 is not an integer). The integrality-preserving native analog is a fixed-quantum LINEAR decrement toward zero, exactly translate's own v -> v + offset[j] step (shape_decode.rs::apply_translate_once, offset=-1) PLUS an absorbing floor at 0 that plain translate does not have (registered explicitly as a deviation, not silently added) -- applied to the ONE in-frame integer quantity the native Hebbian mechanism already holds, evidence_confirm/evidence_disconfirm on a Coactivation ledger (seeds/can_native_reimplementation.json v1.1.0). IDENTITY: a Concept's per-tick sigma reading is a confirm/disconfirm-shaped evidence stream about its OWN typical state, tracked on the SAME evidence-ledger idiom the Hebbian causal-strength axis already uses (own counters, own strictly-later-tick epoch gate, own non-materializing log-odds render) -- the READING half. v1.2.0 (CAN_IDENTITY_FEEDBACK_PREREG.md/_RESULTS.md) closes the FEEDBACK half: can_native_identity_field_feedback writes identity_field FROM that render (fixed 1-quantum step toward the render's sign; neutral/flip-flop decays toward zero via the SAME Max/Min clamp can_native_external_field_decay uses), so can_native_update_3state/_2state's own local-field sum -- which reads identity_field but until v1.2.0 was written by no rule anywhere -- actually feels the identity-evidence axis. Convergence of the discrete-async update WITH this feedback active is measured, not assumed: see CAN_IDENTITY_FEEDBACK_RESULTS.md Sec3 for the real non-convergence count across a real multi-tick draw sample. Both new rules re-express mt_allows(mt, 'allow_h_drift') (self_improvement_loop.py) as a Term (a graph decision, not a Python one) rather than relying on a Python policy check the way the continuous wrappers do. Zero new Rust anywhere in this seed -- Attr/EdgeAttr/Eq/Not/And/Or/Gt/Lt/Plus/Minus/Max/Min/IfThenElse/Log/Div all pre-existed and are reused as-is. See CAN_DECAY_IDENTITY_PREREG.md / _RESULTS.md. v1.1.0 (CAN_EXTERNAL_FIELD_DECAY_PREREG.md/_RESULTS.md) added can_native_external_field_decay, closing CAN_MT_SCOPED_RULES_RESULTS.md Sec4c's remaining maybe_decay_h blocker: external_field is read six times by can_native_update_3state/_2state's own local-field formula but written by no rule anywhere -- that rule was the first writer. Unlike the two rules above, external_field is a SIGNED float with no native accumulation rule (set exogenously, not grown +1 per tick by any rule this arc built), so the existing one-sided integer-floor body (Gt(x,0) then x-1) does not transfer verbatim -- it is generalised (not redesigned) to a symmetric clamp-toward-zero via Max/Min (pre-existing Rust Terms, already used declaratively elsewhere in this tree, e.g. seeds/arousal_window_coreg.json), registered as that rung's one explicit deviation, mirroring how the floor-at-0 deviation from bare translate was registered explicitly in v1.0.0. No same-tick-race guard was needed there (unlike can_native_evidence_decay's own fix): confirmed by direct grep that no native rule, and no Python module including can_counterfactual.py, ever writes external_field -- decay is the ONLY writer that attr ever gets, so there is no reinforcement event to race against. v1.2.0's own same-tick-race check (PREREG Sec3) found the identical structural situation for identity_field -- zero pre-existing writers, so no race guard is needed there either.

attrs.name: evidence_decay
attrs._note: Documents the SHAPE this rung's decay stepping matches (translate, offset=-1 -- toward zero, mirror image of inference_knowledge.json local_id 13's offset=[1] accumulation generator). Declarative only, exactly like logodds_evidence -- never literally invoked at runtime; the actual stepping is ordinary Plus/IfThenElse rule-effect arithmetic (see can_native_evidence_decay). The absorbing floor at 0 is NOT part of translate's own semantics -- an explicit, registered deviation (PREREG Sec1).

attrs.name: identity_evidence
attrs._note: Documents the accumulation half of the identity ledger -- the SAME shape logodds_evidence (inference_knowledge.json local_id 13) already declares for the Hebbian axis, here for the per-Concept sigma-sampling axis (can_native_identity_evidence_sample). Declarative only, not literally invoked.

attrs.name: latent:identity_commitment
attrs._note: The identity-commitment reading's declarative home, mirroring latent:causal_strength's own wiring (inference_knowledge.json local_id 14). No existing rule reads this node -- additive documentation only, matching LOGODDS_GENERATOR_RESULTS.md Sec7 point 2's own precedent (declarative scaffolding, not a consumed mechanism, in this rung).

attrs.name: external_field_decay
attrs._note: v1.1.0 (CAN_EXTERNAL_FIELD_DECAY_PREREG/_RESULTS.md). Documents the SAME translate-toward-zero SHAPE local_id 1 (evidence_decay) declares, applied to external_field -- with ONE registered generalisation: external_field is SIGNED (h in no fixed range, typically set via field_rng.uniform(-1,1) by test/world-adapter code, never accumulated in integer steps by any rule), so the actual stepping (can_native_external_field_decay) clamps SYMMETRICALLY toward zero (max(h-1,0) when positive, min(h+1,0) when negative) via the pre-existing Max/Min Terms, not the one-sided Gt(x,0)-then-x-1 body local_id 1's rule uses (that body relies on x being a non-negative integer, which external_field is not). Declarative only, never literally invoked at runtime -- matching local_id 1/2's own convention.

attrs.name: identity_field_feedback
attrs._note: v1.2.0 (CAN_IDENTITY_FEEDBACK_PREREG/_RESULTS.md). Documents the SAME translate-by-1 SHAPE local_id 1/2/4 already declare, applied to identity_field -- with the sign of the step chosen by the current identity log-odds render, not fixed to a single direction (offset=[1] documents the QUANTUM magnitude only; the actual rule flips the sign via IfThenElse on the render, and falls back to local_id 4's own Max/Min clamp-toward-zero body in the neutral/flip-flop case). Declarative only, never literally invoked at runtime -- matching local_id 1/2/4's own convention.

concepts.name: can_native_evidence_decay
concepts.definition: A native, in-frame-integer-preserving analog of mt_decay_h/mt_decay_J: evidence_confirm/evidence_disconfirm on an already-minted Coactivation ledger each decrement toward zero by exactly 1 per strictly-later external tick (never negative), gated by the SAME allow_h_drift policy axis the continuous mechanism uses -- re-expressed as a graph Term, not a Python decision.
concepts.why: Closes CAN_CONSUMER_MIGRATION_RESULTS.md row 6 blocker (a): decay had no native analog anywhere in this arc before this seed. The continuous h/J decay is multiplicative and cannot preserve an integer count; the integrality-preserving analog is the SAME fixed-quantum step translate already expresses, applied toward zero.

concepts.name: can_native_identity_as_evidence_axis
concepts.definition: A Concept's per-tick sigma reading is a confirm/disconfirm-shaped evidence stream about its OWN typical state, tracked on the SAME evidence-ledger idiom the Hebbian causal-strength axis already uses (own counters, own strictly-later-tick epoch gate, own non-materializing log-odds render) -- the READING half of identity dynamics reuses the already-built mechanism with zero new machinery.
concepts.why: Closes CAN_CONSUMER_MIGRATION_RESULTS.md row 6 blocker (c), BOTH halves as of v1.2.0. The READING half reuses the SAME evidence-ledger idiom the Hebbian causal-strength axis already uses (own counters, own strictly-later-tick epoch gate, own non-materializing log-odds render) with zero new machinery. The FEEDBACK half -- materializing the reading back into identity_field so it participates in can_native_update_3state's own local-field sum, the way the continuous h_id does -- is now BUILT (can_native_identity_field_feedback, CAN_IDENTITY_FEEDBACK_PREREG.md/_RESULTS.md): a fixed 1-quantum step toward the render's sign, its own epoch gate, the SAME policy gate every other rule in this seed uses. Convergence of the discrete-async update with this feedback loop active was measured directly (not assumed) against a real multi-tick draw sample -- see CAN_IDENTITY_FEEDBACK_RESULTS.md Sec3 for the real numbers and verdict.

concepts.name: can_native_external_field_decay
concepts.definition: v1.1.0. A native, in-frame-preserving analog of maybe_decay_h/can_ops.rs::decay_h for the ONE quantity that mechanism targets and this arc had not yet given a native writer: external_field (h), read by can_native_update_3state/_2state's own local-field formula but written by no rule anywhere before this version. Symmetric clamp-toward-zero by exactly 1 per strictly-later external tick (max(h-1,0) when positive, min(h+1,0) when negative, unchanged at 0), gated by the SAME allow_h_drift policy axis maybe_decay_h itself checks -- re-expressed as a graph Term, not a Python decision.
concepts.why: Closes CAN_MT_SCOPED_RULES_RESULTS.md Sec4c's remaining maybe_decay_h blocker (the ONLY one of self_improvement_loop.py's seven operations not migrated for a rule-body reason rather than an orchestration or identity-feedback reason). external_field is signed and has no native accumulation rule (unlike evidence_confirm/identity_evidence_confirm, which are grown +1 by the SAME rule family that decays them), so the existing one-sided integer-floor decay body does not transfer verbatim -- generalised to a symmetric Max/Min clamp, registered explicitly as this rung's one deviation.

concepts.name: can_native_identity_field_feedback
concepts.definition: v1.2.0. A native writer of identity_field, closing the identity-feedback gap can_native_identity_as_evidence_axis's own v1.1.0 'why' field named as unresolved: a fixed 1-quantum step toward the SIGN of the current identity_evidence log-odds render each strictly-later external tick (neutral/flip-flop reading decays identity_field toward zero via the same Max/Min clamp can_native_external_field_decay uses), gated by the SAME allow_h_drift policy axis every rule in this seed checks.
concepts.why: identity_field is read by can_native_update_3state/_2state's own local-field sum but was written by no rule anywhere before v1.2.0 (confirmed by direct grep, CAN_IDENTITY_FEEDBACK_PREREG.md Sec3 -- the SAME class of check CAN_EXTERNAL_FIELD_DECAY_RESULTS.md Sec0 ran for external_field). A magnitude/recurrence-scaled step was investigated and rejected on stability grounds (a growing per-tick bias perturbation threatens the discrete-async update's own Lyapunov convergence argument); a fixed quantum matches every other rule in this seed and was validated against a real convergence sweep before being adopted (CAN_IDENTITY_FEEDBACK_RESULTS.md Sec3).

rules.name: can_native_evidence_decay
rules.comment: Native analog of maybe_decay_h/can_ops.rs::decay_h for the native mechanism's own in-frame evidence_confirm/evidence_disconfirm counters (Coactivation ledger, seeds/can_native_reimplementation.json v1.1.0). Linear (translate, offset=-1) unit decrement toward zero per strictly-later external tick, floored at 0 (translate itself has no clamp -- this rule adds one, registered explicitly, not silently: an evidence count must never go negative). ONE rule bumping BOTH counters via IfThenElse -- not a sibling pair -- reusing CAN_NATIVE_REIMPLEMENTATION_RESULTS.md Sec3's starvation-fix lesson pre-emptively. Policy-gated: mt_allows(mt, 'allow_h_drift'), re-expressed as a Term (PREREG Sec3), same axis the continuous maybe_decay_h uses. See CAN_DECAY_IDENTITY_PREREG.md Sec1 / _RESULTS.md.

rules.name: can_native_identity_evidence_sample
rules.comment: PREREG Sec2: identity dynamics AS a second application of the already-built evidence-axis mechanism (LOGODDS_GENERATOR_RESULTS.md), reading a per-tick sigma stream instead of confirm/disconfirm testimony. Per-Concept ledger (identity_evidence_confirm/_disconfirm/_tick, plain Concept attrs -- identity is single-node, not pairwise, so no Coactivation-style ledger node is needed). ONE rule, IfThenElse-branched -- the SAME starvation-avoidance shape can_native_hebbian_reweight already proved, applied here pre-emptively rather than found broken and fixed. sigma>0 bumps identity_evidence_confirm, sigma<0 bumps identity_evidence_disconfirm, sigma==0 is no evidence (mirrors Hebbian's own state!=0 guard). Policy-gated: mt_allows(mt,'allow_h_drift'), the SAME axis maybe_update_identity/nudge_identity_on_flipped both use. The graded 'commitment' READING is the SAME non-materializing log-odds Term (Log(Div(Plus(confirm,1),Plus(disconfirm,1)))), evaluated live, never written back -- this rule does NOT write identity_field itself -- that write is now done by the SIBLING rule can_native_identity_field_feedback (v1.2.0, CAN_IDENTITY_FEEDBACK_PREREG.md/_RESULTS.md), which reads this rule's own ledger and materializes it into identity_field's feedback role in can_native_update_3state's own local-field sum. This rule's OWN job stays exactly the reading half. See CAN_DECAY_IDENTITY_PREREG.md / _RESULTS.md.

rules.name: can_native_identity_evidence_decay
rules.comment: The SAME linear-decrement-toward-zero shape as can_native_evidence_decay (Rule 1), applied to the per-Concept identity ledger -- demonstrates decay is a reusable RULE SHAPE across both evidence axes this rung builds, not a bespoke mechanism re-derived per axis. Own epoch-gate attr (identity_decay_tick) so this rule's own firing schedule is independent of Rule 2's identity_evidence_tick (sampling and decay are different events and must not share one epoch counter, or a decay tick would be misread as a sample tick or vice versa).

rules.name: can_native_external_field_decay
rules.comment: v1.1.0. Native analog of maybe_decay_h/can_ops.rs::decay_h for external_field (h) -- the ONE quantity that mechanism targets and this arc had not given a native writer (CAN_MT_SCOPED_RULES_RESULTS.md Sec4c). Symmetric clamp toward zero (max(h-1,0) when positive, min(h+1,0) when negative) via pre-existing Max/Min Terms -- the required generalisation of can_native_evidence_decay's one-sided integer-floor body, since external_field is a signed float with no native accumulation rule (PREREG Sec1b). No same-tick-race guard: confirmed by direct grep (PREREG Sec0/Sec2) that no native rule and no Python module (including can_counterfactual.py) ever writes external_field -- decay is the only writer this attr ever gets, so there is no reinforcement event to race against, unlike can_native_evidence_decay's own fix. Policy-gated: mt_allows(mt, 'allow_h_drift'), the SAME axis maybe_decay_h/can_native_evidence_decay/can_native_identity_evidence_decay all use. See CAN_EXTERNAL_FIELD_DECAY_PREREG.md / _RESULTS.md.

rules.name: can_native_identity_field_feedback
rules.comment: v1.2.0. The FEEDBACK half of identity dynamics, closing the gap CAN_DECAY_IDENTITY_RESULTS.md Sec2/CAN_MT_SCOPED_RULES_RESULTS.md Sec5/CAN_EXTERNAL_FIELD_DECAY_RESULTS.md Sec6 all named and explicitly declined to build: writes identity_field FROM the already-built, non-materializing identity log-odds render (can_native_identity_evidence_sample's own confirm/disconfirm ledger), so can_native_update_3state/_2state's own local-field sum (which already reads identity_field six times, seeds/can_native_reimplementation.json lines 166/250/350/434/566/652) actually feels it. DESIGN (CAN_IDENTITY_FEEDBACK_PREREG.md Sec2, registered before this script was run): a FIXED 1-quantum step toward the SIGN of the current logodds render -- logodds>0 -> identity_field+1, logodds<0 -> identity_field-1, logodds==0 (neutral/flip-flop) -> the SAME Max/Min clamp-toward-zero can_native_external_field_decay already uses. A magnitude-scaled (not merely sign-scaled) step -- reusing the render's own ln-scaled magnitude, or nudge_identity_on_flipped's own recurrence-boosted alpha -- was investigated and REJECTED: a per-tick step that GROWS in size is exactly the shape the discrete-async Lyapunov/energy convergence argument (CAN_NATIVE_REIMPLEMENTATION_RESULTS.md Sec2) does not want perturbing its bias term with; a FIXED quantum (same shape as every decay rule in this seed) is the stability-preferred choice, confirmed by the paired convergence sweep (CAN_IDENTITY_FEEDBACK_RESULTS.md Sec3). Own epoch attr (identity_field_tick), independent of identity_evidence_tick/ identity_decay_tick's own schedules. No same-tick-race guard: confirmed by direct grep (PREREG Sec3) that identity_field has ZERO writers anywhere in either native seed before this rule -- this is the FIRST writer, mirroring external_field's own situation exactly. Policy-gated: mt_allows(mt, 'allow_h_drift'), the SAME axis every other rule in this seed uses. Boundedness: under LITERALLY sustained single-direction evidence forever, identity_field grows without a hard cap (no -beta*identity_field decay term is built here, out of scope per the task) -- this mirrors evidence_confirm's OWN existing unbounded-growth design exactly (PREREG Sec2.4), not a new gap; within any finite observed run it is of course bounded, and this rung's live demonstrations report real, finite numbers. See CAN_IDENTITY_FEEDBACK_PREREG.md / _RESULTS.md.
